title: The degree-minus-one standard cotangent boundary cokernel
statement: Let $A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings. Form $R=A[B]$, $Q_1=A[R]$ and $Q_2=A[Q_1]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], with variables $X_b,Y_p,Z_f$ respectively. Let $\epsilon:R\twoheadrightarrow B$ be evaluation and $I=\ker\epsilon$. Define $d_0,d_1:Q_1\to R$ by $Y_p\mapsto p,X_{\epsilon(p)}$, respectively, and augment $Q_1$ to $B$ by their common composite with $\epsilon$. Put $M_1=\Omega^1_{Q_1/A}\otimes_{Q_1}B$, $M_2=\Omega^1_{Q_2/A}\otimes_{Q_2}B$, using the augmentation $Z_f\mapsto\epsilon(d_0f)$ on $Q_2$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. Define the $B$-linear map $\partial_2:M_2\to M_1$ on polynomial differential generators by $\partial_2(\mathrm dZ_f\otimes1)=\mathrm df\otimes1-\mathrm dY_{d_0f}\otimes1+\mathrm dY_{d_1f}\otimes1$. Suppose the rule $\rho(\mathrm df\otimes b)=b[d_0f-d_1f]$ defines a $B$-linear map $M_1\to I/I^2$ with $\rho\partial_2=0$. Let $E=M_1/\operatorname{im}\partial_2$ and denote by $t_p$ the class of $\mathrm dY_p\otimes1$. Then the induced map $\overline\rho:E\to I/I^2$ is a $B$-linear isomorphism, with inverse $[h]\mapsto t_h-t_0$ for $h\in I$. In particular that inverse rule is additive, is linear for the $R$-action through $\epsilon$, and annihilates $I^2$. No finiteness or regularity assumption on $A\to B$ is required.

proof.text: Write $q:M_1\to E$ for the quotient and $D(f)=q(\mathrm df\otimes1)$. The defining formula for $\partial_2$ gives, for every $f\in Q_1$, the relation $D(f)=t_{d_0f}-t_{d_1f}$ in $E$. From the derivation definition [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], $D$ is additive, vanishes on $A$, and satisfies $D(fg)=\epsilon(d_0f)D(g)+\epsilon(d_0g)D(f)$. Also $D(Y_p)=t_p$. These $t_p$ generate $E$ over $B$: the defining presentation of differentials gives generation by all $\mathrm df$; write $f$ as a finite sum of monomials [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] and repeatedly apply additivity and the product rule to express each $\mathrm df$ in the $\mathrm dY_p$.

proof.text: For $f=Y_p$ the relation of step 1 reads $t_p=t_p-t_{X_{\epsilon(p)}}$, hence $t_{X_b}=0$ for every $b\in B$, since $\epsilon(X_b)=b$. Fix $p\in R$, put $b=\epsilon(p)$ and $h=p-X_b\in I$. Apply that relation to $f=Y_p-Y_{X_b}$. Its derivative class is $t_p-t_{X_b}=t_p$, and its two faces are $h$ and $X_b-X_b=0$. Thus $t_p=t_h-t_0$. This will verify one composite of the proposed inverse on every generator.

proof.text: Define the set map $s:I\to E$ by $s(h)=t_h-t_0$. It has $s(0)=0$. For $h,k\in I$, applying step 1 to $Y_h+Y_k$ gives $t_h+t_k=t_{h+k}-t_{2X_0}$. Applying it to $Y_0+Y_0$ gives $2t_0=t_0-t_{2X_0}$, so $t_{2X_0}=-t_0$. Substitution gives $s(h+k)=s(h)+s(k)$. In particular $s(-h)=-s(h)$. Here $0$ as an index means the zero polynomial of $R$, whereas $X_0$ is the variable indexed by zero in $B$; these have not been identified.

proof.text: For $r\in R$ and $h\in I$, use step 1 with $Y_rY_h$. Since $\epsilon(h)=0$, the result is $\epsilon(r)t_h=t_{rh}-t_{X_{\epsilon(r)}X_0}$. The same relation for $Y_rY_0$ is $\epsilon(r)t_0=t_0-t_{X_{\epsilon(r)}X_0}$. Subtracting the two equalities gives $s(rh)=\epsilon(r)s(h)$. Together with step 3, this says that $s$ is $R$-linear when $E$ has its $R$-action through $\epsilon$. No choice of a polynomial lift has entered this formula.

source.place: Tags 08UP (remark-explicit-comparison-map), explicit alternating face boundary, and 08RB (lemma-relation-with-naive-cotangent-complex); agent-written verification of the boundary cokernel.

proof.text: For $h,k\in I$, step 4 gives $s(hk)=\epsilon(h)s(k)=0$. Every element of $I^2$ is a finite sum of products $h_jk_j$ with $h_j,k_j\in I$: coefficients in $R$ can be absorbed into one factor because $I$ is an ideal. Additivity therefore makes $s$ vanish on $I^2$. Define $\sigma:I/I^2\to E$ by $\sigma([h])=s(h)$. If $h-h'\in I^2$, then $s(h)-s(h')=s(h-h')=0$, proving independence of representatives. For $b\in B$, lift it to $r=X_b\in R$; the $B$-action on $I/I^2$ is $b[h]=[rh]$, independent of the lift since another lift differs by an element of $I$. Step 4 gives $\sigma(b[h])=b\sigma([h])$, so $\sigma$ is $B$-linear.

source.place: Tags 08UP (remark-explicit-comparison-map), explicit alternating face boundary, and 08RB (lemma-relation-with-naive-cotangent-complex); agent-written verification of the boundary cokernel.

proof.text: By the assumed identity $\rho\partial_2=0$, the map $\rho$ descends to $\overline\rho:E\to I/I^2$. For every $h\in I$ its composite with $\sigma$ is $\overline\rho(t_h-t_0)=[h-X_0]-[0-X_0]=[h]$; both displayed representatives lie in $I$. Conversely, for every generator $t_p$, with $b=\epsilon(p)$, one has $\sigma\overline\rho(t_p)=\sigma([p-X_b])=t_{p-X_b}-t_0=t_p$ by step 2. Generation from step 1 and $B$-linearity give $\sigma\overline\rho=1_E$. Thus $\overline\rho$ and $\sigma$ are mutually inverse $B$-linear maps, with the inverse rule and its additivity, scalar linearity and vanishing on $I^2$ proved in steps 3--5.

lean.statement: theorem boundary_cokernel_equiv (rho : ModuleOne A B →ₗ[B] (Generators.self A B).toExtension.Cotangent) (rho_formula : ∀ (f : MvPolynomial (MvPolynomial B A) A) (b : B), rho (differentialTensor A B b f) = b • differenceClass A B f) (rho_boundary : rho.comp (boundary A B) = 0) : (∃ e : Cokernel A B ≃ₗ[B] (Generators.self A B).toExtension.Cotangent, e.toLinearMap.comp (LinearMap.range (boundary A B)).mkQ = rho ∧ ∀ h : augmentationIdeal A B, e.symm (Extension.Cotangent.mk h) = inverseRule A B h) ∧ (∀ h k : augmentationIdeal A B, inverseRule A B (h + k) = inverseRule A B h + inverseRule A B k) ∧ (∀ (r : MvPolynomial B A) (h : augmentationIdeal A B), inverseRule A B (r • h) = epsilon A B r • inverseRule A B h) ∧ (∀ h : augmentationIdeal A B, h.val ∈ augmentationIdeal A B ^ 2 → inverseRule A B h = 0)
